rule.name: NSFetchRequest Predicate from User Input
rule.rule_desc: A Core Data predicate may be constructed from external values. Distinguish safely bound values from input that changes predicate format or structure.
rule.vuln_desc: If an attacker controls predicate syntax, they may alter filtering and retrieve records outside the intended selection or authorization boundary.
rule.developer: Keep predicate formats fixed and bind values using the supported placeholder mechanism. Allowlist dynamic fields and enforce record-level authorization independently.
rule.reviewer: Confirm all NSPredicate format strings use proper argument array binding for user-supplied values. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Core Data Store Without Data Protection
rule.rule_desc: The application stores sensitive values or configures protection for persistent data. Determine the actual storage location, backup policy, and lock-state access restrictions.
rule.vuln_desc: An actor with access to unprotected application files, backups, or overly broad keychain access may recover credentials or private records and use them outside the intended trust boundary.
rule.developer: Use the platform credential or key store for secrets and appropriate authenticated encryption and file protection for private records. Minimize stored data, backup exposure, and lock-state accessibility.
rule.reviewer: Confirm Core Data stores containing sensitive data have appropriate file protection levels. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.
